about: Every user-facing feature of this repository, grouped by what it does, with the evidence that it works: the tools it uses, a guide, committed example outputs, the tests that pin them, and independent reviews of those exact outputs (data/reviews.json). A feature is 'proven' only when all of these exist and a passing review's recorded file hashes still match the outputs; otherwise its gaps are listed. docs/FEATURES.md is generated from this file by scripts/feature_catalog.py, which CI checks.

categories.extract: Read a drawing or a structured file into a draft asset model
categories.model: Build a process model from a description, and drawings and exports from a model
categories.export: Hand the model to other systems
categories.check: Check a drawing, a tool or this repository against something independent
categories.operate: Work with live or historical process data, and review the model
categories.screen: Find questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them

features.title: A P&ID image to a draft asset model and review bundle
features.job: Get a starting asset model out of a P&ID without retyping it
features.you_need: One P&ID as a PNG; a model subscription (or the committed example)
features.time: 88 s of commands on one new sheet (sheet 8), measured once; sheet 0's recorded run took 75 s plus 1 s; review time not measured
features.you_get: Extracted symbols, tags and links as a draft model, a review sheet ranked for checking, Ignition tags and PI staging
features.why: Retyping drawings into asset lists takes manual effort in historian, HMI and digital twin projects. A draft turns some of that typing into checking; the time saved has not been measured.

features.title: The one-page report a client reads first
features.job: Show someone what came out of a drawing, and what still needs checking
features.you_need: A review bundle from the step above
features.you_get: One page: the drawing with every item boxed, what is still to check first and why, what a person has already decided (shown with the decision and left out of the to-check list), next steps, limits. Refuses if any generated column of the review sheet doesn't match what the model gives now; the reviewer's OPS_ entries aren't checked, so decisions not yet applied with apply_review.py don't appear
features.why: Whoever approves the work needs one page that says what was found and what is still unchecked, without opening a spreadsheet of 445 rows.

features.title: A DEXPI P&ID file to the same bundle, with no model reading
features.job: Use a DEXPI file my CAD tool already exports
features.you_need: One of the three public DEXPI example sheets, prepared once by adapt_dexpi.py (downloads them; needs PyMuPDF). For your own DEXPI XML, use the DEXPI reader instead
features.time: Seconds once the sheets are prepared
features.you_get: The same bundle with no model reading: tags are the drawn label text, and links are the drawn connections, undirected, with each pipe tee expanded into pairwise links
features.why: A CAD export already represents symbols and connections as data. Reading supported DEXPI content directly avoids a visual model-reading step; conversion limits and omissions still need review.

features.title: Your own DEXPI XML export to a process model with its attributes kept
features.job: Turn the DEXPI XML my CAD tool exports into a model, keeping line sizes, specs and design limits
features.why: A CAD export can hold sizes, specifications and design limits. The reader preserves supported attributes with XML element citations, and reports what it folds, cannot place or drops.
features.you_need: A DEXPI P&ID XML file (tested on DEXPI 1.3, and on DEXPI 1.2 exports from SPPID, Comos, AVEVA and AutoCAD); a rendered PNG only if you also want the drawing bundle
features.you_get: A process model the export, graph and screen tools accept, plus a report of what was kept, folded and dropped, and why

features.title: A written description to a cited model, its exports and a P&ID
features.job: Build a model of a unit that has no usable drawing
features.you_need: A written description (procedure, design basis, report); someone to cite every item
features.time: Writing the model is the work; exports take seconds
features.you_get: Draft review sheet, logical SVGs and Ignition/PI staging from a sourced model; a P&ID also needs an authored layout and drawing dependencies
features.why: A source-cited draft makes an engineer's interpretation of procedures and design notes checkable. Agreement with the actual plant still needs independent records or field evidence and engineering review.

features.title: The model as an open graph of sourced claims
features.job: Load the model into an asset register, graph database or change system
features.you_get: One open JSON graph: assets, typed links in three layers (pipe segments and tees, line networks, and network pairs), every attribute with its source and status; plus a smaller core profile (identity, settings, impact relations and sources) for loading into another system, with everything it leaves out counted
features.why: A plant model is a web of relationships: this transmitter measures that line, this controller moves that valve. Kept as a graph, it answers questions a flat tag list can't, like what a valve's failure affects or which instruments nobody has checked, and other systems can load it without retyping.

features.title: Ignition tags and PI AF staging from a model
features.job: Get the model into Ignition and PI
features.time: Seconds to generate; import is a manual step in a lab gateway
features.you_get: Ignition tag import with UDTs, PI Builder staging sheets; values are placeholders until mapped
features.why: Generating the Ignition tag structure and PI asset staging from one model keeps them consistent with each other and avoids repeated manual entry. Native import still needs a lab check.

features.title: A supplied loop list checked against a drawing key or model
features.job: Compare a supplied loop list with a drawing key or model
features.you_need: A reviewed simple-loop list (controller, measurement, output) and a corresponding drawing key or extracted model
features.you_get: Key: drawn, partly drawn or not drawn; extracted model: tag presence only. Vendor intake example preserves multi-connection functions without inventing loops.
features.why: Controls records and drawings can disagree. Comparing supplied records exposes differences to investigate; current installed behavior still needs site evidence.

features.title: Any digitization tool scored beside perfect, wrong and empty answers
features.job: Find out whether a digitization tool or vendor is actually accurate on our drawings
features.you_need: A few of our sheets labelled by hand, and the tool's output for them
features.time: Seconds once labelled; labelling takes hours
features.you_get: A score beside perfect, wrong and empty answers, per sheet, refusing to report if the scorer can be fooled
features.why: Vendors quote accuracy on their own test drawings. Scoring them on yours, with a deliberately wrong answer scored beside them, shows whether the number means anything.

features.title: Checks a stranger (or their agent) can run on this repository
features.job: Decide whether to trust this repository at all
features.you_need: Python alone for claim and freshness checks; full tests also need pinned packages and required public caches; optional-source omissions are reported separately
features.time: Under a minute for the claim check
features.you_get: Headline claims checked against results files, stage freshness, and selected tests with skipped cases and coverage limits visible
features.why: Before trusting any tool with your plant's data, you should be able to check its claims yourself in minutes.

features.title: Normal bands and an OPC UA replay from historian CSV exports
features.job: Learn normal operating bands from history, or test screens against recorded data
features.you_need: Historian exports as CSV: one of normal running, optionally one of an upset. Standard library only; the replay server also needs asyncua
features.you_get: Bands per tag with false-alarm rates, the first tag to leave its band in an upset, and an OPC UA server replaying the CSV
features.why: History can highlight unusual changes, and replaying recorded data lets you test new screens without touching the live system. Detection before an operational alarm is not guaranteed.

features.title: Reviewer decisions back into the model, and instruments mapped to supplied addresses
features.job: Apply review decisions and assign supplied OPC or PI addresses
features.you_need: A filled review sheet; the plant's I/O list
features.time: Seconds per apply; the review itself is people's time
features.you_get: An updated draft model and dated review record; OPC assignments retain CSV fingerprints and physical line spans, while PI keeps its separate reviewed-point contract
features.why: Source-referenced corrections and addresses make a draft easier to check and hand off. Source records and address assignments do not establish plant truth, connectivity or signal identity.

features.title: Selected workflows checked across registered public inputs
features.job: Find out whether a tool will work on drawings or data like mine, not just the ones it was built on
features.why: A workflow that only saw one set of drawings can fail on the next. Eight selected workflows run across registered applicable inputs, showing where they hold and break, red cells included; other features have their own tests and examples.
features.you_need: Nothing to read the page; the public datasets (fetched by script) to re-run it
features.time: Reading: minutes. Re-running everything: about 25 minutes of cell time, plus downloading the public data once
features.you_get: A pass/fail grid of tools against inputs, the reason for every failure, and the public datasets that would close each gap

features.title: Energy, heat-grade and controls questions worth asking of a drawing, and the data to answer them
features.job: Find energy, heat-grade and control questions worth asking about my unit, and what data answers each
features.why: Many energy and controls questions can be spotted on a P&ID before anyone collects data: a throttled pump, high-pressure steam let down for a low-temperature job, heat dumped to cooling water, a loop with no controller. A solo engineer rarely has time to look. This lists the questions with the evidence by tag and exactly what to collect, and where, to settle each one, without inventing a savings number.
features.you_need: A process model or extracted drawing set; optionally the plant's loop list and equipment schedules
features.you_get: Per question and asset: the evidence by tag, what to collect and where (down to a blank field on a named schedule), how the data decides it, and what public sources say is typical. A screen, not an audit

features.title: First-draft annual energy, cost and CO2e from a measured change, with its assumptions and the data to firm it up
features.job: Turn a change I measured into an annual energy, cost and greenhouse-gas figure
features.why: A measured change becomes a first-draft cost and emissions figure, good enough to decide whether to collect better data, with every constant's source shown and every assumption listed. If you don't have a constant, it tells you exactly which bill, contract or public table has it.
features.you_need: What you measured (kW before and after, steam lb/h, fuel saved, hours) and your tariff, gas price, emission factors and boiler efficiency, or labelled public typical values
features.you_get: A first-draft estimate, marked as one: annual kWh or MMBtu, cost and CO2e with the formula and source of every constant, the assumptions it rests on, and the data to collect (and where) to replace each one; or, per question, what to measure and where each constant comes from

features.title: Every output as plain statements, checked against its source
features.job: Measure how often the model's statements match their sources, and let an operator check a unit in plain English
features.why: "Does this look right?" has no answer you can track. A sampled review of plain sentences against their sources gives an error rate for each kind of statement, and keeps 'matches the drawing' apart from 'true in the plant', which only someone who knows the unit can say.
features.you_need: A graph export (twin-graph-1), plus the sheet image or report PDF its sources cite
features.time: Seconds to render; review time per statement not yet measured
features.you_get: A stratified sample of plain sentences, each beside its drawing crop or report page, with two separate verdict columns; an error rate with a 95% interval; and the verdicts written back into the graph as dated events

features.title: Prepare a first engineering evidence and decision packet
features.job: Build a first evidence and decision packet for company handoff
features.why: A first investigation should leave its question, source revisions, competing evidence and reasons together. Another person can review that packet; a shared company system takes over ongoing ownership and coordination.
features.you_need: A draft model or graph, a question list, local source documents and their revision/locator manifest; an engineer to assign and review answers
features.time: Local packet preparation; engineering review time has not been measured
features.you_get: A local context report, evidence-bound dated decisions and ownership history, unanswered/disputed/stale queues, and versioned JSON plus enriched graph/questions for handoff. The receiving company system supplies shared access and ongoing governance

features.title: Read a selected graph snapshot through bounded internal MCP tools
features.job: Let an approved local assistant retrieve assets, relations and questions from one cleared packet
features.why: A sourced engineering packet becomes reusable through a standard assistant interface while the company keeps authority over its records and decisions.
features.you_need: An approved IT developer environment, optional pinned MCP SDK, and a selected twin-graph-1 JSON snapshot; shared authentication and Copilot reachability require separate work
features.time: Local developer setup; company deployment and engineering review time unmeasured
features.you_get: Six read-only snapshot tools and a summary resource, with source claims, statuses, fingerprints and bounded paging. Public-example SDK/stdio/loopback tests; no source fetching, process-data connector or shared company deployment
